evals.prompt: I need a .NET Kafka producer for Confluent Cloud that sends user signup events with fields: userId, email, planType, signedUpAt. Use the default non-blocking send pattern.
evals.expected_output: A .NET project with a JsonSchemaProducer.cs using the delivery-handler callback (Produce with a callback, serializer wrapped in AsSyncOverAsync), KafkaConfig.cs, Value.cs, AppTests.cs, appsettings.json.example, and a .csproj referencing Confluent.Kafka and Confluent.SchemaRegistry.Serdes.Json. Producer reuses one IProducer instance, registers the JSON schema explicitly with AutoRegisterSchemas=false, targets Confluent Cloud with SaslSsl. Tests pass with dotnet test.
assertions: JsonSchemaProducer.cs is generated
KafkaConfig.cs is generated
The .csproj references the Confluent.Kafka, Confluent.SchemaRegistry, and Confluent.SchemaRegistry.Serdes.Json packages
Value.cs is generated with a UserId property and a [Description] attribute on every property
Producer uses JsonSerializer<Value> from Confluent.SchemaRegistry.Serdes for the value serializer
The serializer passed to Produce() is wrapped with .AsSyncOverAsync() -- NOT passed to Produce() directly as an IAsyncSerializer
Producer sends with a delivery-handler callback (producer.Produce(topic, message, callback)) -- NOT await producer.ProduceAsync(...)
Serializer config sets AutoRegisterSchemas = false
Schema is registered explicitly via RegisterSchemaAsync (or an equivalent ISchemaRegistryClient.RegisterSchemaAsync call) before producing
The Produce helper method accepts an IProducer<TKey,TValue> parameter and does NOT construct a producer inside it
Producer calls `Flush(...)` before the process exits
KafkaConfig builds SecurityProtocol.SaslSsl with SaslMechanism.Plain for KAFKA_ENV=cloud
appsettings.json.example sets KAFKA_ENV to cloud
AppTests.cs is generated and all tests pass with `dotnet test`

evals.prompt: Create a .NET consumer that reads order events from my Confluent Cloud topic and deserializes them with Schema Registry.
evals.expected_output: A .NET project with JsonSchemaConsumer.cs, KafkaConfig.cs, Value.cs, AppTests.cs, appsettings.json.example. Consumer uses JsonDeserializer<Value> wrapped with AsSyncOverAsync, targets Confluent Cloud, and uses a CancellationToken-based shutdown pattern (not Java's wakeup()).
assertions: JsonSchemaConsumer.cs is generated
KafkaConfig.cs is generated
Consumer uses JsonDeserializer<Value> (NOT a raw string deserializer for the value)
The deserializer is wrapped with .AsSyncOverAsync() before being passed to SetValueDeserializer
Consumer uses a CancellationTokenSource / CancellationToken for shutdown -- it does NOT reference Java's consumer.wakeup() or WakeupException
Consumer catches OperationCanceledException and calls Close() in a finally block
ConsumerConfig sets EnableAutoCommit = false and the consumer commits explicitly after processing
The skill does NOT offer or generate a Share Consumer / KafkaShareConsumer-style implementation for .NET
AppTests.cs is generated and all tests pass with dotnet test

evals.prompt: Scaffold a .NET project with both a producer and consumer for IoT sensor readings (deviceId, temperature, humidity, readingTime) on Confluent Cloud.
evals.expected_output: A .NET project with JsonSchemaProducer.cs, JsonSchemaConsumer.cs, KafkaConfig.cs, Value.cs, AppTests.cs, appsettings.json.example, and a .csproj. Both use Schema Registry (JSON Schema default) and Confluent Cloud config.
assertions: JsonSchemaProducer.cs is generated
JsonSchemaConsumer.cs is generated
Value.cs includes a DeviceId property and a Temperature property, each with a [Description] attribute
The .csproj sets <StartupObject> since more than one generated class defines a static Main
Producer uses JsonSerializer<Value> and registers the schema with AutoRegisterSchemas = false
Consumer uses JsonDeserializer<Value> wrapped with .AsSyncOverAsync()
AppTests.cs is generated and all tests pass with `dotnet test`

evals.prompt: I want to try Kafka locally with Docker. Set up a .NET producer and consumer for order events (orderId, customerId, product, quantity, price). This is a batch script so I want to confirm each write lands before moving to the next one.
evals.expected_output: A .NET project with JsonSchemaProducerSync.cs (await ProduceAsync per record), JsonSchemaConsumer.cs, KafkaConfig.cs, docker-compose.yml, Value.cs, AppTests.cs, appsettings.json.example. Uses Plaintext for local Docker.
assertions: JsonSchemaProducerSync.cs is generated and uses await producer.ProduceAsync(...) -- NOT the delivery-handler callback Produce() method
The serializer passed to ProduceAsync is NOT wrapped with .AsSyncOverAsync() -- it is used directly as the async serializer
JsonSchemaConsumer.cs is generated
docker-compose.yml is generated using confluentinc/confluent-local and cp-schema-registry images
docker-compose.yml does NOT invent custom listener names (uses PLAINTEXT, PLAINTEXT_HOST, CONTROLLER)
appsettings.json.example sets KAFKA_ENV to local and SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL to http://localhost:8081
KafkaConfig uses SecurityProtocol.Plaintext with no SASL mechanism set when KAFKA_ENV=local
Value.cs includes an OrderId property
Producer registers the schema explicitly with AutoRegisterSchemas = false
AppTests.cs is generated and all tests pass with `dotnet test`

evals.prompt: I have an order-events topic that carries three event types: OrderCreated, OrderUpdated, and OrderCancelled. I need a .NET producer on Confluent Cloud that can produce all three event types to the same topic. Use Avro since that fits a union schema best.
evals.expected_output: A .NET project with an Avro producer that produces multiple event types to one topic. The Avro schema is a top-level union of records (one per event type), each with an eventType discriminator, registered under order-events-value with TopicNameStrategy (no RecordNameStrategy). The producer and serializer are parameterized over the common ISpecificRecord interface, not one concrete branch type.
assertions: value.avsc defines a top-level Avro union of records (OrderCreated, OrderUpdated, OrderCancelled)
Each union branch record includes an `eventType` discriminator field
Each union branch has a `doc` on the record and on every field
The producer is parameterized as IProducer<string, ISpecificRecord> (or equivalent common interface) rather than one concrete generated class
AvroSerializer<ISpecificRecord> (or the equivalent common-interface type parameter) is used for the value serializer
The skill keeps the default TopicNameStrategy -- it does NOT switch to RecordNameStrategy or TopicRecordNameStrategy
The union schema is registered explicitly under order-events-value with AutoRegisterSchemas = false
The skill mentions avrogen must be run to generate the C# classes from value.avsc before building

The skill points the user to the developing-kafka-java-client skill (or the Java client) as the option that does support Share Consumer
If code is generated at all, it is a regular IConsumer<TKey,TValue> consumer group (JsonSchemaConsumer.cs), not a fabricated queue API
